slides.title: Four words win
slides.text: A passphrase of four random words is long and hard to guess, beating a short word with a number added. Use a different one for every account.
slides.alt: The Pro mailbox key builder: a passphrase made of chosen words, different from every other account key.

focus.cue: Build a mailbox key for Pim from four word tiles
Four random words beat one short word with a number

slides.title: When lists leak
slides.text: In a breach, a service is broken into and its passphrases are copied. Stolen lists are traded, then tried on other accounts to find people who reused a key.
slides.alt: Share or Shield: your mailbox key. Anyone who has it can read your post and send as you, so it stays private.

focus.cue: Your mailbox key: the good side, none; the risk, everything
Public or private? A leaked key must stay private

slides.title: Real keys stay secret
slides.text: Your real passphrase is never for practice. In Packet Post it is called your mailbox key, and you build it by tapping tiles, so nothing real is shared.
slides.alt: The home router still has its key on a sticker anyone can read. Build a new passphrase from four word tiles.

focus.cue: The router's sticker key is public: build it a new one
One tile is the word on the router sticker: never pick it

slides.title: One safe drawer
slides.text: A password manager is the spare-key drawer done properly. It stores a different strong passphrase for each account, so a trusted adult only has to remember one main key.
slides.alt: The backup rule in four steps: make a second copy, keep it in another place, check it opens, keep it fresh.

focus.cue: The backup rule in four steps, in order
Update it, copy it again, check it opens, keep it elsewhere

slides.title: Physical or digital?
slides.text: Sort each measure by what it protects: the machine itself, or the data inside it.
steps: cable lock on a laptop: physical
a passphrase for an account: digital
slides.alt: Physical or Digital: the sort whose bins are the machine and the data, from locked doors to firewalls.

focus.cue: Netville Post protects its mail two ways
Physical you can touch; digital lives in the computers

slides.text: Open Packet Post at Lock It and finish 4 levels. Your passphrase there is called your mailbox key, and you only tap tiles, so nothing real is ever shared.
